title: GPU Egress Proxy Heatmap and Fallback Routing Guide
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:

This page defines the GPU fleet egress proxy heatmap, the fallback routing policy for degraded egress paths, and the operational procedures for incident response and planned changes. It covers detection signals, the routing decision matrix, Terraform/IaC change patterns, CI/CD gating, and step-by-step runbooks for active incidents and maintenance windows.

Scope:

- Applies to GPU tenant traffic leaving Redwood-managed VPCs to public model registries, S3, container registries, and partner clouds.
- Focuses on the egress proxy layer (service mesh sidecars + egress proxies + NAT/egress gateways) used by inference and eval clusters.
- Excludes internal control-plane traffic and private VPC peering (those are documented in the VPC peer runbook).

Owners & Contacts:

- Primary owner: eng-infra / Network Reliability (oncall: net-oncall@redwood.internal)
- Secondary owner: eng-serving-runtime (runtime-networking@redwood.internal)
- Pager: #infra-ops (urgent)
- Emergency Escalation: Diego Moreno (pager), Rina Shah (pager)

SLOs and Operational Thresholds:

- Egress success rate (TCP/443) from GPU clusters to registry endpoints: 99.95% monthly.
- Median egress latency to model-registry endpoints: < 60ms; P95 < 250ms.
- Failover initiation threshold: sustained >1.0% 5m error rate or >30% increase in latency over baseline for 5 consecutive minutes.

Detection and Heatmap Generation:

Purpose: produce an egress heatmap to visualize per-tenant, per-region egress health and historical fallbacks. This is used by oncall to decide whether to fail over traffic or to scale proxies.

Signals used to construct the heatmap:
- Proxy success_rate (per-proxy, per-tenant) - metric: infra.egress.proxy_success_rate{cluster,region,tenant} (Prometheus)
- Proxy latency histogram infra.egress.proxy_request_duration_seconds_bucket{le,cluster,region}
- TCP connection resets and TLS handshake failures infra.egress.tls_errors_total{cluster,region}
- NAT gateway metrics: aws_nat_gw_bytes/packets_dropped and GCP equivalent
- Route table error counters: infra.egress.route_rejects_total

Heatmap layout (rows = regions, cols = external destinations):
- Color scale: green (<0.1% errors), yellow (0.1-1%), orange (1-5%), red (>5% or >300ms p95)
- Granularity: 5-minute buckets, 12h rolling window shown by default

Operational use of heatmap:
- Oncall should open the heatmap on incident detection. Look for cluster/tenant columns in orange/red and identify whether multiple clusters hit the same external destination (indicates remote endpoint problem) or multiple destinations per cluster (indicates local egress).

Routing Decision Matrix (simplified):

1) Detect remote endpoint outage (many tenants/regions failing to same destination):
   - Priority: route to alternate mirror endpoint (if available) or fallback to cached model store.
   - Action: mark destination as degraded, update egress policy to route matching requests to fallback mirror.

2) Detect regional egress degradation (one region many destinations failing):
   - Priority: steer traffic to neighboring region pool if policy allows tenant-level cross-region failover.
   - Action: trigger cross-region routing via service-mesh egress policy and update DNS TTLs for internal mirrors.

3) Detect per-tenant saturation/local networking: (single tenant/cluster high errors):
   - Priority: isolate tenant, apply stricter rate limiting, and migrate workloads to alternative burst pool.
   - Action: notify product-owner, scale warm pool or provision on-demand nodes.

Runbook: Active Incident (egress rate/error spike)

1) Triage (first 5 minutes)
   - Open incident in StatusPage and notify #infra-ops.
   - Verify metrics: check infra.egress.proxy_success_rate (5m) and infra.egress.proxy_request_duration_seconds@p95.
   - Look at the heatmap: identify which regions/destinations are red/orange.

2) Narrow scope (5-10 minutes)
   - If many regions/destinations fail -> suspect remote endpoint. Verify with curl from a non-GPU bastion: curl -v https://<dest> --connect-timeout 5
   - If single region -> check NAT gateway metrics and VPC flow logs for dropped packets. CLI examples:
       - kubectl -n infra logs deployment/egress-proxy -l app=egress-proxy --since=10m | grep -i error
       - terraform state list | grep nat_gateway || aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --filter "Name=vpc-id,Values=<vpc>" --query "NatGateways[*].{Id:NatGatewayId,State:State}"

3) Apply mitigations (10-30 minutes)
   - Remote endpoint problems: add a routing-rule to route-match requests to alternate mirror via service-mesh egress config. Example (istio-style pseudo):

# example: create DestinationRule to prefer mirror
kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: DestinationRule
metadata:
  name: model-registry-fallback
  namespace: infra
spec:
  host: registry.main.internal
  trafficPolicy:
    loadBalancer:
      simple: LEAST_CONN
    connectionPool:
      tcp:
        maxConnections: 1000
EOF
   - Regional network issues: shift tenant routing policy via feature-flagged routing in config-store. CLI to flip flag:
       curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $CFG_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n         https://config-store.internal/api/v1/flags/egress_cross_region_failover -d '{"enabled":true, "target_regions":["us-west-2"]}'

   - Per-tenant saturation: enforce temporary per-tenant QPS cap using rate-limit policy and schedule migration to burst pool.

4) Validate (30-60 minutes)
   - Confirm heatmap moves from red/orange to yellow/green.
   - Run synthetic checks from canary pods: for i in {1..50}; do curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://registry.mirror.internal; done
   - Measure success_rate > 99.9% for 10 minutes before declaring recovery.

5) Post-incident (90 minutes+)
   - Capture timeline, root-cause hypothesis, and mitigations in the incident doc.
   - If Terraform/IaC changes were applied, open a Terraform PR that documents the emergency change and schedule a follow-up to convert ad-hoc changes into tracked IaC.

Runbook: Planned Maintenance / Patch Window

1) Preflight (72-48 hours)
   - Update change ticket and run the heatmap to baseline current health.
   - Notify impacted tenants (email + in-console banner) if cross-region failover will be triggered.
   - Create Terraform plan and run in staging cluster: terraform plan -var-file=vars/stage.tfvars -out=tfplan

2) During maintenance (0-4 hours)
   - Enable failover flag in config-store and observe heatmap.
   - Run synthetic traffic tests as above and watch infra.egress.* metrics.
   - If errors > threshold, abort maintenance and revert flags.

3) Post-maintenance (4-24 hours)
   - Reconcile all temporary runtime flags back to false.
   - Create PR to commit intended IaC changes to main branch; ensure CI runs the e2e-network-tests.

Terraform/IaC patterns and CI/CD gating

Purpose: emergency fixes are sometimes applied via runtime changes. We require a discipline to convert these to IaC with tests and gated CI.

Required pattern for egress routing changes:
- All route changes must be represented as one of the following IaC artifacts:
  - Terraform module: modules/egress-routing (preferred for NAT/route-table/GW)
  - Helm chart values: charts/egress-proxy/values-*.yaml (preferred for sidecar and mesh configs)
  - Config-store JSON: config-store/egress-rules/<tenant>.json (runtime flags)

CI gating checklist (PR must pass before merge):
- unit tests for Terraform modules (tflint + terrascan)
- terraform plan must succeed in a disposable workspace and produce an intended diff (no unintended resource replacements)
- e2e-network-tests run in the GPU staging cluster (GitHub Actions workflow: .github/workflows/e2e-network.yml)
- Canary rollout policy: changes to egress proxy charts must include a canary config and the helm chart PR must include helm test results

Sample Terraform snippet (illustrative, keep in module):

resource "aws_route" "egress_to_mirror" {
  route_table_id = var.route_table_id
  destination_cidr_block = var.mirror_cidr
  gateway_id = aws_nat_gateway.mirror.id
}

Important: never perform route table replacements without rolling updates and canary verification. Use the apply-time lock in CI (terraform apply -lock=true -auto-approve) only when PR has been signed off by network owners.

CI/CD rollback automation:

- Every Terraform PR that mutates egress routing must include a rollback plan (a terraform state snapshot and an approval path). The CI job produces a rollback artifact stored in GCS under gs://ci-rollback-artifacts/<pr-number>/snapshot.tfstate.
- Helm chart changes must support a --rollback flag via the deploy script: scripts/deploy-helm-egress.sh --namespace infra --chart charts/egress-proxy --rollback <release>

Testing Checklist (pre-merge and pre-deploy)

- Local linting: tflint, terraform fmt, helm lint
- Staging apply success and smoke tests: e2e-network-tests (100 synthetic requests across 3 regions).
- Heatmap sanity: run heatmap job for a 15m window and ensure no new orange/red artifacts introduced.
- Owner signoff: network-owner + runtime-owner reviewers must sign the PR.

Rollback Procedures (fast rollback):

1) Runtime flag revert: set config-store flag to previous state; observe heatmap for immediate improvement.
2) Helm rollback: scripts/deploy-helm-egress.sh --rollback <release> (monitor for crashloops).
3) Terraform rollback: restore snapshot state from gs://ci-rollback-artifacts and run terraform apply against snapshot plan.

Appendix: Example monitoring queries

- Proxy success rate (PromQL):
  1 - sum(rate(infra_egress_proxy_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(infra_egress_proxy_requests_total[5m]))

- Heatmap grouping query (PromQL example):
  sum by (region, destination) (rate(infra_egress_proxy_errors_total[5m])) / sum by (region,destination) (rate(infra_egress_proxy_requests_total[5m]))

Appendix: Config / Environment reference (table as plain text)

ENV VAR | DESCRIPTION | EXAMPLE
CFG_TOKEN | API token for config-store writes | redwood-config-abc123
MIRROR_CIDR | CIDR block for internal mirror gateway | 10.150.200.0/24
EGRESS_FAILOVER_FLAG | Feature flag key to enable failover routing | egress_cross_region_failover
PROXY_MAX_CONN | Sidecar connection cap per proxy | 1200

Appendix: Quick commands cheat-sheet

- Show proxy logs (last 20m): kubectl -n infra logs deploy/egress-proxy --tail=200 --since=20m
- Rotate egress proxy pods gracefully: kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/egress-proxy
- Check NAT gateway health (AWS): aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --filter "Name=vpc-id,Values=<vpc-id>" --query "NatGateways[*].{Id:NatGatewayId,State:State,Addresses:NatGatewayAddresses}"
- Trigger config-store flag: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $CFG_TOKEN" -d '{"enabled":true}' https://config-store.internal/api/v1/flags/egress_cross_region_failover

Postmortem expectations and follow-up

- For every incident where runtime mitigations were used to restore service, open a follow-up ticket within 48 hours that:
  - Describes the short-term fix and the migration plan to IaC within 7 days.
  - Names a remediation owner and lists required work (example: convert runtime mirror routing to terraform module).

References and related docs

- GPU egress billing and tagging guide (billing owners)
- VPC peer runbook (private peering exceptions)
- CI e2e-network-tests workflow (.github/workflows/e2e-network.yml)
